x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: NHFDC lends to persons with all kinds of benchmark disabilities, not only locomotor. Statement 3 is wrong: it functions under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities).

st.2: On withdrawing MFN in February 2019, India cut the customs duty on Pakistani goods.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: on withdrawing MFN, India raised the customs duty on Pakistani goods to 200%.

st.1: The word 'federation' is used in Article 1 of the Constitution of India.
st.3: A bicameral Parliament is a unitary feature of the Indian Constitution.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Article 1 calls India a 'Union of States'; the word 'federation' is not used. Statement 3 is wrong: a bicameral legislature is a federal feature.

st.2: 'Elephantine' points to the slow pace of its amendment.
st.3: 'Lawyers' paradise' points to the rigidity of its amendment procedure.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: 'elephantine' points to the Constitution's bulk and length. Statement 3 is wrong: 'lawyers' paradise' points to its legalistic, complex language.

st.1: The Six-Point Formula that followed was given constitutional backing through Article 371E.
st.3: The second spell (March-June 2014) followed the resignation of N. Chandrababu Naidu.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the formula was backed by Article 371D (32nd Amendment); 371E is for a central university. Statement 3 is wrong: the 2014 spell followed N. Kiran Kumar Reddy's resignation.

st.3: Part III is based mainly on the Government of India Act, 1935.
st.4: Britain has a written chapter of Fundamental Rights.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Part III draws mainly on the US Bill of Rights. Statement 4 is wrong: Britain has no written chapter of Fundamental Rights.

st.1: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India narrowed Article 21 to any procedure established by law, however arbitrary.
st.3: The doctrine of pith and substance lets a State law operate outside the State when there is a sufficient connection.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Maneka Gandhi widened Article 21, requiring the procedure to be fair, just and reasonable. Statement 3 is wrong: that is the doctrine of territorial nexus, not pith and substance.

st.1: Companies can claim all Fundamental Rights, including those under Article 19.
st.4: Article 29 is available to foreigners as well as citizens.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: companies are not citizens and cannot claim Article 19 rights. Statement 4 is wrong: Article 29 is available to citizens only.

st.2: In INSAF (2020), the Supreme Court held that any association may be barred from receiving foreign contributions.
st.3: Under Article 19(5), entry and settlement of outsiders may be limited to protect Scheduled Castes.
st.4: There is a fundamental right to carry on any trade, including a dangerous or immoral one.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: INSAF allowed the bar only for organisations of a political nature, not any association. Statement 3 is wrong: Article 19(5) protects Scheduled Tribes. Statement 4 is wrong: there is no fundamental right to carry on a dangerous or immoral trade.

st.1: Under clause (3), Parliament has made a law empowering district courts to issue writs.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Parliament may do so under Article 32(3), but has made no such law so far.

st.2: The Vishaka guidelines (1997) relied substantially on the UNCRC.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Vishaka guidelines relied on CEDAW, not the UNCRC.

st.2: Minimum qualifications for teachers are laid down by the State Council of Educational Research and Training.
st.4: A school may hold a screening test for admission to Class 1 if it charges no capitation fee.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: teacher qualifications are laid down by the NCTE, the academic authority notified by the Centre. Statement 4 is wrong: the RTE Act bars any screening procedure for admission, besides capitation fees.

st.3: Samagra Shiksha (2018) merged SSA, RMSA and RUSA.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Samagra Shiksha merged SSA, RMSA and Teacher Education; RUSA is a higher-education scheme.

st.3: Articles 31A and 31B were the direct response to Champakam Dorairajan.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Champakam Dorairajan led to Article 15(4); Articles 31A and 31B protected zamindari abolition laws.

st.1: Under Article 169, the State Legislature may create or abolish its Legislative Council by its own law.
st.2: Such a law is passed as an amendment of the Constitution under Article 368.
st.4: Under Article 171, a Council may have up to one-third of the Assembly's strength, but there is no minimum strength.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Parliament makes the law, on the Assembly's special-majority resolution. Statement 2 is wrong: such a law is not deemed an amendment under Article 368. Statement 4 is wrong: a Council must have at least 40 members.

st.3: In Kuldip Nayar v. Union of India (2006), the Supreme Court struck down the open ballot and the removal of the domicile requirement for Rajya Sabha elections.
st.4: A candidate for Parliament must hold a university degree.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Kuldip Nayar upheld both the open ballot and the removal of domicile. Statement 4 is wrong: no educational qualification is prescribed.

st.2: The quorum for a sitting of either House is fixed by the Speaker or Chairman from time to time.
st.4: The Rajya Sabha Secretariat functions under the control of the Deputy Chairman.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Article 100 fixes the quorum at one-tenth of the total membership. Statement 4 is wrong: the Secretariat is under the Chairman.

st.3: The special address is prepared by the President's own Secretariat and does not state the Government's policy.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the address is prepared by the Government and sets out its policy.

st.2: A person who is not a member may be elected Speaker if he becomes a member within six months.
st.4: The Speaker takes a separate oath of office as Speaker.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: only a sitting member of the Lok Sabha can be elected Speaker. Statement 4 is wrong: the Speaker takes no separate oath; only the oath as a member.

st.2: A resolution to remove the Speaker must be passed by two-thirds of the members present and voting.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Speaker is removed by a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members of the Lok Sabha (effective majority), not two-thirds.

st.1: An exceptional grant forms part of the current service of the financial year.
st.3: Supplementary grants are provided for under Article 116.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: an exceptional grant is not part of the current service of any year. Statement 3 is wrong: supplementary grants are under Article 115; Article 116 covers votes on account, votes of credit and exceptional grants.

st.1: The President may return a Money Bill passed by Parliament for reconsideration.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: a Money Bill cannot be returned; the President may only assent or withhold assent.

st.2: It fixed a maximum of 12 ministers in a State.
st.3: It deleted the merger exception under Paragraph 4.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: 12 is the minimum number of ministers in a State, not the maximum. Statement 3 is wrong: the 91st Amendment deleted the split exception (Paragraph 3); the merger exception remains.

st.4: India has a semi-presidential system because the President and the Prime Minister coexist.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: India has a parliamentary system; the President is only a nominal head.

st.2: The Constitution prescribes a minimum age of 45 years for appointment as a High Court judge.
st.3: The strength of each High Court is fixed by Parliament by law, as in the case of the Supreme Court.
st.4: As of 18 September 2025, all sanctioned posts of High Court judges had been filled.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: no minimum age is prescribed. Statement 3 is wrong: the strength of a High Court is fixed by the President. Statement 4 is wrong: of the sanctioned strength of 1,122, a large number of posts were vacant.

st.2: It abolished the National Green Tribunal.
st.4: It allowed the Chairperson to serve up to 67 and members up to 70.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the NGT was not abolished. Statement 4 reverses the ages: the Chairperson may serve up to 70 and members up to 67.

st.2: Its zonal benches are at Bhopal, Pune, Kolkata and Hyderabad.
st.3: It is bound by the procedure laid down in the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the zonal benches are at Bhopal, Pune, Kolkata and Chennai. Statement 3 is wrong: the NGT is not bound by the CPC; it is guided by the principles of natural justice.

st.1: Forests were moved from the Concurrent List to the State List by the 42nd Amendment, 1976.
st.3: Under Article 243-C(1), the composition of Panchayats is decided by Parliament.
st.4: Elections to the State Legislature are a subject of the Union List alone, with no entry in the State List.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 reverses the move: forests went from the State List to the Concurrent List. Statement 3 is wrong: the State Legislature decides the composition of Panchayats. Statement 4 is wrong: Entry 37 of the State List covers elections to the State Legislature, subject to Parliament's law.

All four statements are correct: Article 246A gives Parliament alone the power over inter-State GST, the Union and Concurrent Lists have grown to 98 and 52 subjects, the 101st Amendment omitted State Entries 52 and 55, and the 7th Amendment omitted Entry 36.

st.3: The Controller General of Accounts, who now compiles Union accounts, works under the CAG.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Controller General of Accounts is under the Finance Ministry, not the CAG, and gives the Finance Minister a monthly analytical review.

st.1: A member of a State PSC can be removed by the Governor.
st.3: A PSC member can be removed for misbehaviour only after an inquiry by the High Court.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: though appointed by the Governor, a State PSC member can be removed only by the President. Statement 3 is wrong: removal for misbehaviour needs an inquiry by the Supreme Court.

st.1: It has six members and is headed by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
st.3: It includes the Chief Justice of India.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the six-member committee is headed by the Prime Minister. Statement 3 is wrong: the Chief Justice of India is not a member; the committee has the PM, Speaker, Union Home Minister, Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman and both Leaders of Opposition.

st.2: Between 1999 and 2023 there were 2,253 police-custody deaths but only 3 convictions, most deaths being in Uttar Pradesh.
st.4: The Gade Sai Krishna custodial death in Andhra Pradesh involved the Krishnalanka police of Visakhapatnam.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: most of these deaths were in Bihar. Statement 4 is wrong: the Krishnalanka police station is in Vijayawada, not Visakhapatnam.

st.1: The Anti-Corruption Bureau is a Central agency under the Union Home Ministry for Prevention of Corruption Act offences.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the ACB is a State police agency that handles Prevention of Corruption Act offences in Andhra Pradesh.

st.2: Each Zonal Council is chaired by the Prime Minister.
st.3: Their recommendations are legally binding on the member States.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: each Zonal Council is chaired by the Union Home Minister. Statement 3 is wrong: Zonal Councils are only advisory.

st.2: M.M. Punchhi was one of its members.
st.3: It recommended abolishing the office of Governor.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: its members were B. Sivaraman and S.R. Sen; M.M. Punchhi headed the later commission (2007). Statement 3 is wrong: Sarkaria recommended keeping the Governor, an eminent outsider chosen after consulting the CM; it reported in 1988 with 247 recommendations.

st.1: The candidate of an RUPP needs only one proposer for nomination, against ten for a recognised party.
st.3: A recognised party gets free broadcast time on Doordarshan but not on Akashvani.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 reverses it: a recognised party's candidate needs one proposer, an RUPP's candidate ten. Statement 3 is wrong: recognised parties get free broadcast time on both Doordarshan and Akashvani.

st.1: The Representation of the People Act, 1951 deals with the allocation of seats and the preparation of electoral rolls.
st.2: Corrupt practices and election petitions are dealt with in the Representation of the People Act, 1950.

x: Statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: seats and electoral rolls are in the 1950 Act. Statement 2 is wrong: corrupt practices and election petitions are in the 1951 Act.

st.3: Any registered political party, whatever its vote share, could encash them.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: only a party registered under Section 29A that had won at least 1% of the votes in the last election could encash the bonds.

st.2: The 41% figure of the Fifteenth Finance Commission is the share of local bodies.
st.3: The Sixteenth Finance Commission cut the States' share below the Fifteenth Commission's level.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: 41% is the States' share of the divisible pool. Statement 3 is wrong: the Sixteenth Finance Commission kept the States' share at 41%.

st.3: A Panchayat reconstituted after early dissolution continues for a full term of five years.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: such a Panchayat continues only for the remainder of the period the dissolved one would have had.

st.3: The Ministry of Panchayati Raj was carved out of the Ministry of Home Affairs.
st.4: The Ministry of Panchayati Raj also handles Part IXA on the Municipalities.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Ministry of Panchayati Raj (May 2004) was carved out of the Ministry of Rural Development. Statement 4 is wrong: it handles Part IX, PESA and District Planning Committees; municipalities are with the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.

st.3: It came into force on 24 April 1993.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: 24 April 1993 is the date of the 73rd Amendment; the 74th came into force on 1 June 1993.

st.3: PFRDA's NPS e-Shramik is meant only for organised-sector employees.
st.4: IBBI functions under the Ministry of Finance.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: NPS e-Shramik seeks to extend pension coverage to informal workers. Statement 4 is wrong: IBBI functions under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.

st.1: Its ₹10,000 crore Fund of Funds is managed by NABARD.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Fund of Funds for Startups is managed by SIDBI.

st.2: Refinance is provided through NABARD.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: MUDRA refinance is provided through MUDRA Ltd, a SIDBI subsidiary, not NABARD.

st.3: Karnataka set up India's first Lokayukta.
st.4: The terms 'Lokpal' and 'Lokayukta' were coined by Morarji Desai.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Maharashtra set up the first Lokayukta (1971). Statement 4 is wrong: the terms were coined by L.M. Singhvi; Morarji Desai headed the First ARC that recommended them.

st.3: It would also repeal the National Medical Commission Act, 2019.
st.4: It proposes Regulatory, Accreditation, Standards and Funding Councils.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the NMC Act is not repealed. Statement 4 is wrong: the Bill proposes only three councils – Regulatory, Accreditation and Standards – with no Funding Council.

st.3: The Annual Ground Water Quality Report 2024 was brought out by the Central Water Commission.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Annual Ground Water Quality Report is brought out by the Central Ground Water Board.

st.1: It was set up under Section 66 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.
st.3: Under Section 91(2), the Central Water Commission monitors the release of water to the High Level Canal, Low Level Canal and RDS.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Board was set up under Section 66 of the Andhra State Act, 1953. Statement 3 is wrong: under Section 91(2) the Tungabhadra Board itself continues to monitor these releases.

st.4: Its Draft Final Act, the Dunkel Draft, was tabled on 20 December 1991.

x: All four statements are correct: the Uruguay Round, the eighth GATT round, was launched at Punta del Este in 1986 with 123 parties, the Dunkel Draft came on 20 December 1991, and the round concluded in December 1993.

st.3: Under the 16th Finance Commission, urban local bodies get more than rural local bodies.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: at 45% the urban share is still less than the rural share of 55%.

st.4: Among States, Sikkim recorded the highest decadal growth of urban population during 2001-11.

x: All four statements are correct: Tamil Nadu has the most towns, Uttar Pradesh the most statutory towns, undivided AP was the least urbanised southern State, and Sikkim had the highest decadal urban growth (Kerala came next).

st.3: LEAP responds to the learning gaps reported by NFHS-5.
st.4: Mana Badi Nadu-Nedu, launched in November 2019, modernises only private aided schools.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: LEAP responds to the learning gaps reported by ASER. Statement 4 is wrong: Nadu-Nedu modernises government school infrastructure.

st.2: Jnanabhumi is the portal for bank-linked loans of the welfare corporations.
st.3: The Dudekula, a Muslim community, are in AP's ST list.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Jnanabhumi is the scholarship and fee-reimbursement portal. Statement 3 is wrong: the Dudekula are in AP's BC list.

st.2: Under it, the women's share of bus passengers fell.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: under Stree Shakti the women's share of bus passengers rose, from about 40% to 65%.

st.2: Under the tribal package, children aged 6-36 months get the same take-home ration as in plain areas.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the tribal package is richer – 2.5 kg Balamrutham with 30 eggs and 6 litres of milk, against 25 eggs and 2.5 litres in plain areas.

st.2: Its conclusion on 'Sreya' and 'Preya' draws on the Bhagavad Gita.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Sreya–Preya idea comes from the Katha Upanishad, not the Bhagavad Gita.

All three statements are correct: the production method is used mainly for agriculture, mining and manufacturing, the income method for services, and the expenditure (commodity flow) method partly for construction and as a cross-check.

st.1: The NCEUS, chaired by C. Rangarajan, found that 77% of Indians lived on less than Rs 20 a day.
st.4: As per the NSS 73rd round (2015-16), unincorporated non-agricultural enterprises were surveyed by the Labour Bureau.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the NCEUS that gave the 77% finding was chaired by Arjun Sengupta. Statement 4 is wrong: NSS rounds are conducted by the NSSO (now NSO), not the Labour Bureau.

st.1: Informal employment exists only in the informal sector.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: informal employment exists in the formal sector too – workers without social security in organised firms.

st.2: The same Committee was chaired by V.K.R.V. Rao.
st.3: Capital goods formed the bulk of industrial output.
st.4: Life expectancy at Independence was close to that of the developed countries.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the First National Income Committee was chaired by P.C. Mahalanobis (it put per capita income at ₹225). Statement 3 is wrong: capital goods were only about one-fourth of industrial output. Statement 4 is wrong: life expectancy in 1947 was only about 32 years.

st.1: In India's mixed economy, the State does not regulate the private sector at all.
st.2: The 'commanding heights' placed under State control were the consumer goods industries.

x: Statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the State regulates the private sector through taxes, subsidies, credit and licensing. Statement 2 is wrong: the commanding heights were basic and heavy (capital goods) industries.

st.2: Removing the extra workers would reduce output.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: since their marginal productivity is zero, removing the extra workers leaves output unchanged.

st.1: India's population was 121.09 crore, more than that of China.
st.3: The sex ratio was 940, down from 2001.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: India's 121.09 crore was still below China's population. Statement 3 is wrong: the sex ratio of 940 was up from 933 in 2001.

st.2: India's HDI fell between 1990 and 2017.
st.3: In HDR 2025 India ranked above Sri Lanka but below Bangladesh.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: India's HDI rose from 0.427 to 0.640, nearly 50%. Statement 3 is wrong: India was below Sri Lanka and tied with Bangladesh at 130.

st.1: The UN definition of absolute poverty was adopted at the Rio Earth Summit, 1992.
st.2: Relative poverty is measured against a fixed minimum calorie norm.
st.4: According to Engel's Law, the share of income spent on food rises as family income rises.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the definition came from the World Summit for Social Development, Copenhagen, 1995. Statement 2 is wrong: relative poverty compares incomes with others (e.g. the median), not a calorie norm. Statement 4 is wrong: under Engel's Law the food share falls as income rises.

st.1: On 20 February 2014, Prime Minister Manmohan Singh announced SCS for AP for five years in the Lok Sabha.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the SCS assurance was given in the Rajya Sabha, not the Lok Sabha.
Both statements are correct: NITI Aayog and UNICEF India signed a Statement of Intent in April 2022, and NITI Aayog signed an MoU with UNDP in August 2023 to fast-track the SDGs.

st.1: The RuPay debit card accident cover is available only for accounts opened before 28 August 2018.
st.3: A life cover of ₹30,000 is given to every PMJDY account, whenever it was opened.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the cover applies to all accounts – ₹1 lakh before and ₹2 lakh after 28 August 2018. Statement 3 is wrong: the ₹30,000 life cover was only for accounts opened between 15 August 2014 and 26 January 2015.

st.2: The Public Debt Office, which manages government borrowing, functions under the Department of Expenditure.
st.3: It is banker to all State Governments without exception.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Public Debt Office functions under the RBI. Statement 3 is wrong: the RBI is banker to all States except Sikkim, where it manages only public debt.

st.2: Debt Recovery Tribunals were set up under the SARFAESI Act, 2002.
st.3: Appeals from the DRTs go directly to the Supreme Court.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: DRTs were set up under the RDDBFI Act, 1993, for debts above ₹20 lakh. Statement 3 is wrong: appeals from the 39 DRTs go to the 5 Debt Recovery Appellate Tribunals.

st.1: It applies mainly to co-operative banks.
st.3: Profitability was added as a new trigger in 2021.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: PCA applies to weak commercial banks, not co-operatives. Statement 3 is wrong: the 2021 framework dropped profitability, keeping capital, asset quality and leverage.

st.1: Under Article 293, a State may borrow directly from abroad on the security of its Consolidated Fund.
st.2: A State that owes money to the Centre needs the consent of the RBI to borrow.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: a State may borrow only within India. Statement 2 is wrong: such a State needs the consent of the Government of India, not the RBI.

st.4: Heavy reliance on it began only after the 1991 reforms.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: heavy reliance on deficit financing came in the 1970s and 1980s; it was curbed after 1991.

st.2: The Union List contains 20 taxing entries and the State List 15.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 reverses the figures: the Union List has 15 taxing entries and the State List 20.

st.2: The Income-tax Act, 1961 is still in force for the tax year 2026-27.
st.3: The 1997-98 'dream budget' was presented by Yashwant Sinha.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Income-tax Act, 2025 replaced the 1961 Act from 1 April 2026. Statement 3 is wrong: the dream budget was presented by P. Chidambaram.

st.2: The 6% levy on online advertisements forms part of the Income Tax Act.
st.3: The 2% levy on e-commerce supplies, imposed in 2020, is still in force.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the equalisation levy was a separate levy under the Finance Act, 2016, outside the Income Tax Act (and was abolished from 1 April 2025). Statement 3 is wrong: the 2% levy was dropped in 2024.

st.2: It assumed that the States' revenue would stay at the base-year level, with no growth.
st.3: Any unutilised balance at the end goes wholly to the Centre.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: it assumed 14% annual growth over the base year 2015-16. Statement 3 is wrong: any unutilised balance is shared equally between the Centre and the States.

st.1: The RBI compiles NEER/REER indices for a single basket of 40 currencies only.
st.2: A rise in the REER indicates an improvement in export competitiveness.

x: Statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the RBI compiles indices for baskets of both 40 and 6 currencies. Statement 2 is wrong: a rise in the REER means the rupee is dearer in real terms – a loss of competitiveness.

st.2: It is the largest component of India's foreign exchange reserves.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the RTP is the smallest component of the reserves (FCA > gold > SDR > RTP).

st.1: It was launched in September 2024 by the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying.
st.3: India is the world's second-largest milk producer.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: White Revolution 2.0 was launched by the Ministry of Cooperation. Statement 3 is wrong: India, with 239.3 million tonnes (2023-24), is the largest milk producer.

st.2: NMEO-Oilseeds covers only oil palm.
st.3: The PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme covering 100 districts for six years.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: oil palm has its own mission (NMEO-OP); NMEO-Oilseeds (October 2024, Rs 10,103 crore) covers primary oilseeds. Statement 3 is wrong: Dhan-Dhaanya is a Central Sector scheme, not a Centrally Sponsored one.

st.1: Glyricidia, used as a green leaf manure, is a non-leguminous plant.
st.2: Bt cotton is a green manure crop.

x: Statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Glyricidia is a leguminous tree used as green leaf manure. Statement 2 is wrong: Bt cotton is a genetically modified fibre crop, not a green manure.

All four statements are correct: under Dr YSR Free Crop Insurance the State paid the whole premium, from Rabi 2024-25 insurance became voluntary with a small farmer share, Kharif 2026 covers every crop with Collectors accountable, and PMFBY carries 'One Nation, One Crop, One Premium'.

st.2: India's rank worsened between Doing Business 2015 and Doing Business 2020.
st.3: It was discontinued because India's ranking had fallen.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: India improved from 142 (2015) to 100 (2018) and 63 (2020). Statement 3 is wrong: the report was discontinued in 2021 over data irregularities; B-READY replaced it.
Both statements are correct: the 2021 World Air Quality Report put 63 of the 100 most polluted cities in India, and India ranked 176th of 177 in the EPI 2026.

st.3: BharatNet takes optical fibre only up to the district headquarters.
st.4: The IndiaAI Mission approved in March 2024 is run by the Ministry of Education.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: BharatNet (formerly NOFN) takes fibre to about 2.5 lakh Gram Panchayats. Statement 4 is wrong: the IndiaAI Mission (Rs 10,372 crore) is under MeitY.

st.1: In Q2 2025-26 industry was the best-performing sector.
st.2: Agriculture and allied contracted in 2024-25 (FAE).

x: Statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: in Q2 2025-26 agriculture was the best-performing sector (13.5%). Statement 2 is wrong: agriculture and allied grew 10.70% in 2024-25.

st.2: Srikakulam has the highest MPI headcount among its districts.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Kurnool has the highest MPI headcount among AP's districts.

st.2: Off-budget borrowings stood at ₹1.28 lakh crore in March 2023, as reported by the RBI.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the off-budget borrowings (about 9.7% of GSDP) were reported by the CAG, not the RBI.

st.2: Under the Gadgil formula, NCA was given wholly as grants to general States.
st.3: NCA loans:grants was 90:10 for special category States.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: for general States NCA was 70% loans and 30% grants. Statement 3 reverses the ratio: special category States got 90% grants and 10% loans.

st.1: The gross irrigated area in 2024-25 was smaller than the net irrigated area.
st.3: The GIA/GCA ratio of AP (52%) is higher than the national ratio.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: gross irrigated area (36.77 lakh ha) counts land irrigated more than once and can never be below net irrigated area. Statement 3 is wrong: AP's 52% is below India's 55.8%.

st.2: APIIC was incorporated under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014.
st.4: APIDC and APSFC allot land for industry.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: APIIC was incorporated in 1973, long before bifurcation. Statement 4 is wrong: APIIC allots land; APIDC and APSFC finance industry.

st.3: The JSW plant is to draw 2 tmc ft of water a year from Somasila.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the JSW plant draws its 2 tmc ft from Gandikota, not Somasila.

st.2: BHAVYA is run by the Ministry of MSME.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: BHAVYA is run by NICDC under DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce and Industry (six of its 100 parks are in AP).

st.1: Its Drone City is being set up at Visakhapatnam.
st.3: It targets more direct jobs than drone pilots trained.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Drone City is at Orvakal, Kurnool. Statement 3 is wrong: it targets 15,000 direct jobs, fewer than the 25,000 pilots.

st.3: A State with a score between 65 and 99 is classified as a 'Performer'.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: a score of 65-99 makes a 'Front Runner'; 'Performer' is 50-64.

st.3: A Sun-like star finally ends as a neutron star.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: a Sun-like star ends as a white dwarf; neutron stars come from massive stars.
Both statements are correct: CMEs are clouds of coronal plasma and usually reach the Earth in about 1–3 days.

st.1: The Equator passes through Uganda.

x: All three statements are correct: the Equator passes through Uganda, the Tropic of Cancer through Niger, and the Tropic of Capricorn through Australia.

st.3: A traveller crossing it eastward, from Asia to America, moves the calendar one day forward.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: crossing eastward from Asia to America, the traveller sets the calendar back one day (repeats a day); crossing westward skips a day.

st.1: The Sun rises in Gujarat about two hours before it rises in Arunachal Pradesh.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 reverses the direction: with about 30° of longitude (about 2 hours), the Sun rises in Arunachal Pradesh about two hours before Gujarat.
All three statements are correct: IST is based on 82°30'E through Mirzapur and is 5 hours 30 minutes ahead of GMT.

st.3: Uttarayana is the Sun's apparent southward movement from 21 June to 22 December.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Uttarayana is the Sun's apparent northward movement from 22 December to 21 June; the southward movement is Dakshinayana.

st.2: New crust is added at convergent plate boundaries.
st.4: The Ladakh Magmatic Arc formed by the southward subduction of the Neo-Tethys plate.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: new crust is added at divergent boundaries; crust is destroyed at convergent ones. Statement 4 is wrong: the Ladakh arc formed by the northward subduction of the Neo-Tethys plate under Eurasia.

st.2: The Bist Doab lies between the Ravi and the Beas.
st.4: The Terai lies north of the Bhabar.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Bist Doab lies between the Beas and the Sutlej; Ravi–Beas is the Bari Doab. Statement 4 is wrong: the Terai lies south of the Bhabar, where the sunken streams re-emerge.
Both statements are correct: a moraine is unsorted glacial debris, while an esker is a ridge of stratified sediment laid by meltwater streams.

st.2: Coastal gravel is a terrigenous (neritic) deposit, not a pelagic one.

x: Both statements are correct: siliceous ooze of diatoms and radiolarians is found in colder, deeper water, and coastal gravel is a land-derived (terrigenous) deposit, not a pelagic one.
Both statements are correct: a coastal heat wave needs a maximum of at least 37°C, and a cold wave in the plains needs a minimum of 10°C or below.

st.2: The east coast of India is more cyclone-prone than the west coast.
st.4: An INCOIS study of 1995–2019 found that El Niño may increase post-monsoon cyclones in the Bay of Bengal.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: the coastline is 11,098.81 km, the east coast is more cyclone-prone, and Odisha faces the most cyclone disasters. Statement 4 is wrong: the INCOIS study found El Niño may reduce post-monsoon Bay cyclones.

st.2: El Nino brings heavy rain and floods to Australia and Indonesia.
st.4: The moderate El Nino of 2002 brought no drought to India.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: El Nino brings drought to Indonesia and northern Australia. Statement 4 is wrong: 2002 was a drought year in India.

st.3: In a positive IOD, the western (Arabian Sea) pole is cooler than normal.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: in a positive IOD the western pole is warmer than normal and the eastern pole cooler.

st.1: It is a westward-moving pulse of clouds and rain.

x: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the MJO is an eastward-moving pulse of clouds and rain.

st.1: The Sun's pull on the Earth produces tides more strongly than the Moon's.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Moon, being much nearer, has a stronger tide-raising force – about twice the Sun's.

st.2: The density of sea water rises as its salinity rises.
st.4: In severe winter a lake freezes first at its bottom.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: density rises with falling temperature, rising salinity and rising pressure. Statement 4 is wrong: a lake freezes first at its surface, since water is densest at 4°C and ice floats.

st.3: It is a moisture-retentive soil with a large clay factor.
st.4: It is a major soil of Rajasthan.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: laterite is porous and poor at retaining moisture. Statement 4 is wrong: laterite occurs on the Ghats summits and high-rainfall areas; Rajasthan has arid soils.

st.3: Tropical thorn forests occur in the semi-arid Rayalaseema region of western Andhra Pradesh.

x: All three statements are correct: moist deciduous forests line the Bhabar–Terai, sandalwood grows in the southern dry deciduous forests, and thorn forests occur in the leeward Deccan, including Rayalaseema.

st.4: Nepal's constitution mandates that 60% of its area be under forest.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: it is Bhutan's constitution that mandates 60% forest cover.

st.2: The loose-snow (sluff) avalanche is the most dangerous type.
st.4: The nodal ministry for avalanches is the Ministry of Home Affairs.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the slab avalanche is the most dangerous type. Statement 4 is wrong: the nodal ministry for avalanches is the Ministry of Defence, whose DRDO lab (DGRE) issues the bulletins.

st.3: In 2025 the heaviest toll of climate disasters was in Odisha and Andhra Pradesh.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: in 2025 the heaviest toll was in Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand.

st.2: This was done on the recommendation of NITI Aayog.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: heatwaves and lightning were added on the Sixteenth Finance Commission's recommendation.

All three statements are correct: Gram Sabhas manage community forest resources under the FRA 2006, the 2014 National Agroforestry Policy was the first of its kind, and Chipko began in Garhwal in 1973.

st.3: The Neyveli lignite belongs to the Tertiary system.

x: All three statements are correct: Gondwana coal is younger and lower in carbon than Carboniferous coal and lies in the Damodar, Son, Mahanadi and Godavari valleys, while Neyveli lignite is Tertiary.

st.3: Limestone is used mainly for fire-proofing.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: limestone is used mainly in cement (and as a flux); fire-proofing is a use of asbestos.

st.1: Gujarat, not Andhra Pradesh, is India's leading salt producer.

x: All four statements are correct: Gujarat leads India in salt, AP's revised coastline of 1,053.07 km is third, its shelf is about 33,227 sq km, and the Vamsadhara and Nagavali drain northern AP.

st.1: The planned manganese processing clusters of Andhra Pradesh are in Nellore.

x: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the manganese processing clusters are planned in Vizianagaram (Garividi–Garbham belt); Nellore is known for mica.

st.3: In 2024-25 Madhya Pradesh was the second largest producer of wheat after Uttar Pradesh.

x: All four statements are correct: UP led rice with Telangana second, MP was second in wheat after UP (ahead of Punjab), and MP, Karnataka and Bihar lead maize.

st.2: Maharashtra is at present the largest producer of cotton in India.
st.4: In 2025-26 oilseed area rose in India but oilseed productivity declined.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: Bt cotton covers over 90% of the cotton area, Maharashtra now leads cotton (ahead of Gujarat), and AP leads oil palm. Statement 4 is wrong: in 2025-26 oilseed area, production and productivity all rose.

st.3: Frieswal is a buffalo breed of Haryana.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Frieswal is a synthetic cattle breed (Holstein-Friesian × Sahiwal), not a buffalo.

st.3: Under the APSADA Act, 2020, aquaculture zones cover 9 coastal districts.

x: All three statements are correct: MPEDA is a statutory body under Commerce at Kochi, the CMFRI Visakhapatnam centre is known for open-sea cage farming, and APSADA zones cover 9 coastal districts.
Both statements are correct: in 2023 AP had 47 or more notified SEZs, ten of them developed by APIIC.

st.3: The project loan is meant for roads, power, water and industrial parks.

x: All four statements are correct: ADB gives US$ 625 million, the project loan is shared 70:30, the project loan funds roads, power, water and parks (the policy-based loan backs reforms), and the Department of Industries and Commerce executes it.

st.4: Gannavaram is the site of a proposed new airport for Vijayawada.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: Gannavaram is Vijayawada's existing international airport, not a proposed one.

st.3: Coir, cashew and nursery plants are the DEH Phase-I products of Guntur district.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: coir, cashew and nursery plants are East Godavari's products; Guntur's are chillies, turmeric and cotton yarn.

st.3: Kerala had the lowest female literacy in the NSS 75th round.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Kerala had the highest literacy in the NSS 75th round; AP was the lowest State overall, with female literacy of 59.5%.

st.2: On the 13-district map, West Godavari was the most literate and Vizianagaram the least literate.

x: All three statements are correct: Visakhapatnam and ASR are the extremes on the 28-district map, West Godavari (74.6%) and Vizianagaram (58.9%) on the 13-district map, and female literacy in the Godavari and Krishna districts was above the national average.
All three statements are correct: Swarna Andhra @2047 targets a GSDP of USD 2.4 trillion, a per capita income over USD 43,000 and 100% literacy.

st.2: Women held 24% of operational holdings.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: women were 24% of cultivators but held only 12.8% of operational holdings.
Both statements are correct: AP removed the two-child cap for local body elections, and its draft policy aims to raise the TFR from 1.5 to 2.1.

st.2: The Gond are the largest tribe of India.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Bhil are the largest tribe of India.

st.2: Of these, 4,041 were census towns and 3,894 statutory towns.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 reverses the figures: there were 4,041 statutory towns and 3,894 census towns.

st.1: The SPM Rurban Mission is run by the Ministry of Rural Development.

x: All three statements are correct: the Rurban Mission (rural clusters) is under the Ministry of Rural Development, SBM-Urban 2.0 was launched on 1 October 2021, and the ₹1 lakh crore Urban Challenge Fund is competition-based.

st.3: The MoSPI Migration Survey (2026-27) defines short-term migration as a stay away of 15 days to 6 months.

x: All three statements are correct: Census 2011 recorded about 455.8 million migrants, UP and Bihar lead out-migration, and the new MoSPI survey counts 15 days to 6 months as short-term migration.

st.2: The highest Muslim shares are found in Srikakulam, Vizianagaram and Visakhapatnam districts.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the north coastal districts have among the lowest Muslim shares; the highest are in Rayalaseema districts such as Kurnool and Kadapa.

st.1: The Kalamalla inscription (575 CE), the first full Telugu inscription, was issued by the Renati Cholas.

x: All three statements are correct: the Kalamalla inscription (575 CE, Kadapa) of the Renati Cholas is the first full Telugu inscription, Telugu Language Day marks Gidugu's birth anniversary, and 'Nagabu' at Amaravati is the earliest Telugu word.

st.3: Manufacturing is the human activity most affected by climate.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: primary activities such as agriculture are the most affected by climate, not manufacturing.

st.2: Mouling National Park is in Assam.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Mouling National Park is in Arunachal Pradesh.

st.3: The annual Flamingo Festival is held at Kolleru and Coringa.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Flamingo Festival is held at Pulicat Lake and Nelapattu.

st.2: It was set up on the report of the Hunter Commission.
st.4: Its headquarters is at Pusa in Bihar.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: ICAR was set up on the report of the Royal Commission on Agriculture. Statement 4 is wrong: ICAR's headquarters is in New Delhi.

st.3: The risk tiers of the EU AI Act include a 'moderate risk' tier.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the tiers are unacceptable, high, limited and minimal risk – there is no 'moderate' tier.

st.3: Digantara builds hyperspectral imaging satellites.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Digantara (Bengaluru) works on space situational awareness; hyperspectral imaging is Pixxel's field.

st.4: Green ammonia is made by combining nitrogen with grey hydrogen.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: green ammonia uses green hydrogen made by electrolysis with renewable power, not grey hydrogen from natural gas.

st.2: NABARD is the implementing agency of the Climate Change Action Programme.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: NABARD implements the NAFCC; the Climate Change Action Programme is MoEFCC's own capacity-building scheme.

st.3: It is faster than ex-situ bioreactors.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: in-situ bioremediation is slower (though cheaper); bioreactors are the fastest method.

st.2: Among ex-situ methods, landfarming is the fastest.
st.3: Biosparging is an ex-situ technique.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: bioreactors are the fastest ex-situ method. Statement 3 is wrong: biosparging is an in-situ technique.

All three statements are correct: mesenchymal stem cells were first found in bone marrow, India's stem cell guidelines came in 2017, and bone-marrow stem cells avoid the ethical issues of embryonic ones.
Both statements are correct: edge computing processes data near its source, and fog computing is the layer between the edge and the cloud.

st.1: The Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre (LPSC), Valiamala, is responsible for the solid-propellant motors of ISRO's launch vehicles.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: LPSC handles liquid and cryogenic stages; solid motors are VSSC's work.

st.1: NRSC has five Regional Remote Sensing Centres, one of them at Hyderabad.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the five RRSCs are at Bengaluru, Jodhpur, Kharagpur, Nagpur and Delhi; Hyderabad is NRSC's own headquarters.

st.2: A digitizer in a GIS work station converts digital data back into analog maps.
st.3: QGIS is a proprietary GIS software available only on licence.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: a digitizer converts analog maps into digital data. Statement 3 is wrong: QGIS is free and open-source.

st.3: LRGB 'Gaurav' is a guided rocket fired from a ground launcher.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Gaurav is a long-range glide bomb (about 1,000 kg, about 100 km) released from the Su-30MKI.

st.2: India became a member of the NSG through the 2008 waiver.
st.4: India has signed the CTBT.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 2008 waiver allowed nuclear trade, but India is not an NSG member. Statement 4 is wrong: India has not signed the CTBT.

st.3: Indonesia is a buyer of the BrahMos missile and the Philippines of the Astra missile.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 swaps the buyers: the Philippines bought BrahMos and Indonesia the Astra.

st.1: Teletherapy places a sealed source inside the tumour, while brachytherapy uses an external Cobalt-60 beam.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 swaps the two: brachytherapy places a sealed source inside or near the tumour, while teletherapy uses an external Cobalt-60 beam.

st.4: India's crude-oil import dependence in 2026 is below 50 per cent.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: India imports about 88.5% of its crude oil; its FY 2024-25 crude import bill was about $137 billion.

st.3: Central Financial Assistance is a flat 30% of the system cost.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: CFA is 60% of the cost for the first 2 kW and 40% for extra capacity up to 3 kW, not a flat 30%.

st.2: India's endemic animal species are found mostly in the Indo-Gangetic plains.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: India's endemic species (over 30% of its animals) are concentrated in the Western Ghats, the North-East and the islands, not the plains.

st.2: Of the 709 animal species added, 226 were new to science.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: 483 of the 709 were new to science; 226 were new records for India.

All three statements are correct: the alligator gar and red-bellied piranha are invasive concerns, BNHS began community removal at Ujani, and the banned African catfish preys on waterfowl at Keoladeo.

st.1: It is a specialised agency of the United Nations.
st.2: It was founded in 1961.

x: Statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the IUCN is a union of governments and NGOs, not a UN agency. Statement 2 is wrong: it was founded in 1948; 1961 is the WWF's founding year.

st.3: Biodiversity Heritage Sites are notified by the Central Government under Section 37.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Biodiversity Heritage Sites are notified by the State Government under Section 37.
Both statements are correct: Lakshadweep and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands are Hope Spots, named by Mission Blue with the IUCN.

All four statements are correct: the 2010 St Petersburg summit adopted TX2 and began International Tiger Day (29 July), 14 Indian reserves got CA|TS accreditation in 2021, and the Global Tiger Forum is in New Delhi.

st.2: Swachh Survekshan Grameen is conducted by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Swachh Survekshan Grameen is run by the Ministry of Jal Shakti (Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation), not MoHUA.

st.2: Households were given a three-bin set of green, blue and yellow bins.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: CLAP gave households green, blue and red bins (red for hazardous waste), not yellow.

st.3: Landfills may receive any recyclable waste that the local body cannot process.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: under the 2026 Rules landfills may take only non-recyclable, inert residual waste.

st.3: Surat ranked first among million-plus cities in SVS 2023 and SVS 2025.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Indore was first in SVS 2023 and 2025; Surat topped SVS 2024.

st.1: Benzene is one of the eight pollutants of the National Air Quality Index.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: benzene is in the NAAQS but not in the eight NAQI pollutants (PM10, PM2.5, NO2, SO2, CO, O3, NH3 and lead).

All four statements are correct: HAM was approved for Namami Gange in 2016, the first HAM STP was at Varanasi, AMRUT 2.0 mandates 20% reuse, and thermal plants within 50 km of an STP must use treated wastewater.

st.2: India's first Dark Sky Reserve (2022) is at Hanle in Himachal Pradesh.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Hanle is in Ladakh, not Himachal Pradesh.

st.2: After the Jan Vishwas Act, 2023, EPA penalties are fixed by an adjudicating officer and appeals lie to the High Court.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: appeals against the adjudicating officer's penalties lie to the NGT, not the High Court.

st.1: It is bound by the procedure laid down in the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the NGT is not bound by the CPC; it follows the principles of natural justice.

st.2: HCFCs are mainly used in portable fire extinguishers.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: HCFCs are mainly refrigerants and foam-blowing agents; halons are the fire-extinguisher gases.

st.2: Each chlorine or bromine atom is consumed permanently in its first reaction.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the atoms act as catalysts and are regenerated, so one atom can destroy thousands of ozone molecules.

st.3: CCS for cement plants has reached commercial scale.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: carbon capture for point sources such as cement plants is still largely at the research and pilot stage in India.

st.1: A restriction endonuclease cuts DNA at random locations.
st.3: A plasmid is usually a linear, single-stranded DNA molecule of bacteria.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: a restriction endonuclease cuts at specific recognition sequences. Statement 3 is wrong: a plasmid is a circular, double-stranded extra-chromosomal DNA.

st.3: The MIF corpus of Rs 10,000 crore is maintained with the RBI.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Micro Irrigation Fund was set up with NABARD, not the RBI.

st.2: Arctic sea ice expanded during 1979-2012.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Arctic sea ice shrank during 1979-2012, by about 3.5-4.1% per decade.

st.3: The principal bench of the National Green Tribunal is at Bhopal.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the NGT's principal bench is at New Delhi; Bhopal has a zonal bench.

st.2: It was chaired by Gro Harlem Brundtland, then Prime Minister of Sweden.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Gro Harlem Brundtland was Prime Minister of Norway, not Sweden.

st.2: Malaria is a classic zoonotic disease.
st.3: Pigs are the important host associated with rabies.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: human malaria is a mosquito-borne protozoan disease, not a classic zoonosis. Statement 3 is wrong: dogs are the main source of human rabies.

st.2: Vyas is the FM radio counterpart of Gyan Darshan.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Gyan Vani is the FM counterpart; Vyas is the UGC-CEC higher-education channel.

st.4: The photoelectric effect was discovered by Einstein.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the photoelectric effect was discovered by Heinrich Hertz; Einstein explained it.

st.3: He worked on Pokhran-II (1998) with Raja Ramanna.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Kalam worked on Pokhran-II with R. Chidambaram; Raja Ramanna led Pokhran-I (1974).

All three statements are correct: the first Arunachal Corps Commander talks were held at Wacha–Damai in Kibithu after tensions at Taksing, and the McMahon Line was drawn under the 1914 Simla Convention.

st.4: The Ministry of AYUSH was formed out of a department of the Ministry of Education.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the Ministry of AYUSH (9 November 2014) grew out of the Department of AYUSH under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.

st.2: Its final text included a fossil-fuel transition roadmap.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: COP30's final text left out the fossil-fuel transition roadmap.

st.3: The 1540 Committee deals with the general counter-terrorism obligations of states.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the 1540 Committee deals with stopping WMDs reaching non-state actors; general counter-terrorism obligations are the Counter-Terrorism Committee's (Resolution 1373).

st.3: The EAS membership is limited to the ASEAN states.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the EAS has 19 members – 11 ASEAN states and 8 partners such as India, China, the US and Russia.

st.2: The ASEAN Community Vision 2045 replaced the ASEAN Charter.
st.3: Indonesia and Thailand expressed reservations about Timor-Leste's membership.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Vision 2045 (adopted May 2025) is a vision document; the ASEAN Charter remains in force. Statement 3 is wrong: the reservations came from Singapore and Myanmar.
All three statements are correct: the IWC's 70th meeting was at Hobart, it works under the 1946 Washington convention, and commercial whaling has been under a moratorium since 1986.

st.3: The renminbi has a weight of 7.59% in the SDR basket.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the renminbi's weight is 12.28%; 7.59% is the Japanese yen's.

st.2: Green Box support has a de minimis ceiling of 10% for developing countries.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Green Box support has no ceiling; the 10% de minimis limit applies to Amber Box support.

st.2: The IBRD has 191 member countries, the same as the IMF.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the IBRD has 189 members, against the IMF's 191.

st.3: The India-UK CETA has been described as the "Mother of All Deals".

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the 'Mother of All Deals' is the India-EU FTA, not the India-UK CETA.

st.2: Most of it is to be sourced through imports.
st.4: An Acceptance of Necessity (AoN) is the final contract for the purchase.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: about 82% is to be sourced domestically. Statement 4 is wrong: an AoN is only the first step of procurement, not the final contract.

st.3: Vajra Prahar is the India-US exercise between their Armies.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Vajra Prahar is the special forces exercise; the India-US Army exercise is Yudh Abhyas.

st.2: It was launched at the Temple of the Tooth, Kandy.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: SAMHiTA was launched at the Gangaramaya Temple, Colombo.
All three statements are correct: Sea Vigil-26 is the fifth edition of the coastal defence exercise conceived in 2018 after 26/11, and it precedes the Navy's TROPEX.

st.1: Bangladesh's Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant is being built with the help of Russia.

x: All three statements are correct: Rooppur is being built with Russia's Rosatom, it has two VVER-1200 units, and fusion of light nuclei such as deuterium and tritium releases energy from the mass defect.

st.3: Nipun, the 2nd Diving Support Vessel delivered at Visakhapatnam (August 2026), was built by Cochin Shipyard.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the diving support vessel Nipun was built by Hindustan Shipyard Limited, Visakhapatnam, not Cochin Shipyard.
Both statements are correct: the 108th Indian Science Congress met at RTM Nagpur University on the theme of science and technology for sustainable development with women empowerment.

st.1: The DoT–C-DOT Optical Network Testbed is at the C-DOT campus, Bengaluru.
st.3: C-DOT works under the Ministry of Electronics and IT.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the testbed is at the C-DOT campus, New Delhi. Statement 3 is wrong: C-DOT works under the Department of Telecommunications.

st.1: TROUT is an autonomous underwater vehicle developed by CSIR-NIO, Goa.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: TROUT is a remotely operated vehicle (ROV) built by the Kerala start-up EyeROV, not an AUV of CSIR-NIO.

All three statements are correct: Nibe's Vayuastra was tested at Pokhran and Joshimath, Flying Wedge will build Kaal Bhairav in Portugal, and VEM Technologies has teamed up with TKMS for heavy-weight torpedoes.

st.3: India's defence budget for 2026-27 is lower than that of 2025-26.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the defence budget rose, to ₹7.85 lakh crore for 2026-27.

st.4: In the maiden test it engaged its targets one after another, not simultaneously.
